text:
Evgeni Malkin is 40, in the last year of his contract, and still one of the better play drivers in hockey when he's healthy. He has 18 points in 19 games, and with him on the ice at five on five the Penguins have taken 54% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances. Right now, though, he's out with an upper-body injury; he missed games against Nashville and Dallas and skated in a non-contact jersey at practice Monday.

His last ten games tell the familiar story: one goal, ten assists. He set up teammates at a rate Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put in the 96th percentile last season, and 55% of his own shots came off the rush. Evolving-Hockey's numbers add the old trade-off: his team created far more with him on, and gave up more too, bottom 4% of forwards defensively.

Our range for his scoring sits above his current pace, so there's nothing here that looks like luck running out. What to watch is the return date, and what Pittsburgh decides about a pending free agent who is still producing like a first-line center.
